budget_items.what_was_said: The town transferred money from cemetery sale of lots to a different fund within the cemetery, as part of the consent calendar.

The town raised and appropriated funds for the town accountant line and transferred salary-reserve funds to fund the new police union contract, the accountant, police department, IT department, and assessor's line.

budget_items.topic: Finance department turnover and consulting costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said the finance director, assistant accountant, and payroll/benefits coordinator all left, requiring consultants to keep operations running, driving the article 2 request.
The town manager said the FY26 audit was budgeted lower than the auditor now expects to charge.
The town manager said positive cherry sheet (state aid) and new-growth changes, offset by recap adjustments, left a surplus available to appropriate at this meeting.
The town manager said Lunenburg failed to timely bill 11 Fitchburg-served water accounts, and Fitchburg charges 14% interest on late amounts owed under the intermunicipal agreement.

budget_items.topic: Prior-year Fitchburg payment funding sources (article 3, part 1)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town proposed transferring unexpended capital funds from two old articles plus raising the remainder to pay Fitchburg's FY25 bill.

budget_items.topic: Ritter ADA ramp original capital funding (article 3 context)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said the original ADA ramp project at Ritter was funded years ago but has not proceeded and may be redesigned.
The town manager said the water enterprise fund was underbudgeted and future rate adjustments or transfers may be needed.

budget_items.topic: Water enterprise revenue shortfall / tax rate risk
budget_items.what_was_said: The finance director said the town only collected a fraction of the budgeted water revenue because billing lapsed, which could complicate certifying the tax rate.
The town manager stated the stabilization fund balance as of June 30 in response to a question about funding the Fitchburg bill from it.

budget_items.topic: Total Fitchburg amount owed and paid
budget_items.what_was_said: The finance director gave the FY25 total owed to Fitchburg, the amount already paid, and the remaining balance.
The town paid small outstanding prior-year bills to Haywood Hospital, Advanced Print Technology, and CBiz (an FY24 audit bill).
The town transferred previously appropriated capital funds to hire a new consultant to help establish a storm water utility fee structure.

budget_items.topic: MS4 storm water compliance cost gap
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said the operating budget cannot fund MS4 permit compliance and estimated the additional annual amount needed.
The DPW director projected a quarterly per-homeowner storm water fee if the utility is established.
The DPW director said the DPW operational budget was reduced this year, making it unlikely the town could add the funds needed for MS4 compliance through the regular budget.
The DPW director gave three years of prior spending on the storm water consultant that produced outdated impervious-area data.
The town created a pooled fund for the facilities directors to hire outside estimators, citing a Ritter building estimate that was far too low.

budget_items.topic: Net school spending vs. actual budget gap
budget_items.what_was_said: The presenter said the gap between the state's net school spending formula and the district's actual operating budget, driven largely by out-of-district placement costs, is large.
A school committee member said the circuit breaker balance could absorb roughly one unexpected placement.
A school committee member said out-of-district placement costs and student counts have both risen sharply over several years.
A school committee member gave earlier-year out-of-district placement costs and student counts to show the multi-year trend.

budget_items.topic: Prior bill vote as example of budget strain
budget_items.what_was_said: A school committee member cited the earlier $90,000 Fitchburg vote as an example of what an unfunded emergency does to the process.
A school committee member said this same town meeting cycle had already funded additional money for a new student who entered the district.

budget_items.topic: Senior property tax deferral income limit (article 9)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town proposed indexing the senior deferral income eligibility limit to the state circuit breaker limit instead of a fixed cap, and had earlier cut the deferral interest rate.

budget_items.topic: Town meeting warrant printing and mailing cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager presented the calendar-year cost of printing and mailing the full warrant booklet to every household for both 2025 meetings, as the rationale for switching to postcards.
The town manager said moving current employees to a new vacation-accrual system requires a one-time buyout of banked time above a cap for 13 staff.

minutes.headline: Town meeting reversed a failed vote to pay Fitchburg the water bills Lunenburg forgot to send for over a year
minutes.summary: This special town meeting worked through 17+ warrant articles, most contentiously a near-failed then reconsidered vote to pay Fitchburg for water bills the town had failed to send to 11 accounts for over a year, plus a $195,790.97 FY26 budget amendment driven by heavy finance-department staff turnover. Town meeting also funded a storm water utility consultant and a capital cost-estimating fund, created a special education out-of-district reserve fund, raised the senior tax-deferral income limit, adopted an MBTA Communities Act zoning overlay at Tritown, revised SAP personnel/benefit rules, passed over a Kids Kingdom playground transfer and a warrant-mailing change amid public pushback, and narrowly voted down eliminating the town's volunteer personnel committee.

what_happened.line: Town meeting rejected, then reconsidered and passed, paying Fitchburg for water bills the town failed to send to 11 accounts for over a year.
Town meeting approved a mid-year FY26 budget amendment driven by turnover of the finance director, assistant accountant, and payroll coordinator.
Town meeting created a special education out-of-district reserve fund over the finance committee's own recommendation against it.
Town meeting adopted a zoning overlay at Tritown to comply with the state's MBTA Communities Act.
Town meeting narrowly voted to keep the volunteer personnel committee rather than dissolve it.

why_it_matters: The Fitchburg billing lapse left the water enterprise fund short of budgeted revenue, which the finance director said could complicate setting the tax rate, and it is the reason a related capital-fund transfer needed town meeting approval at all.

The new special education reserve fund is a standing account town meeting still controls dollar by dollar, meant to absorb the swings in out-of-district placement costs that have come up in three straight budget seasons.
The MBTA Communities zoning overlay is a compliance vote, not a building proposal by itself, but it sets the multifamily density allowed at Tritown going forward.
